options: How much of the input energy becomes useful output
How big the fuel tank is
questions.explanation: Efficiency is the useful share of the input — everything not useful leaves as heat, sound, or drag.
questions.misconception: Some mistake it for speed or max power; it's a ratio of useful to total.

questions.prompt: An engine takes 200 J in and outputs 60 J of useful work. What is its efficiency?
questions.misconception: Leaving out the 100 (0.3) or dividing the wrong way (200 ÷ 60 ≈ 333%) are classic slips.

questions.prompt: Why is the efficiency of a real machine always below 100%?
options: Some input energy always escapes as heat, sound, and waste
Machines are made lazy on purpose
Energy gets heavier as it works
It hits exactly 100% when a machine is new
questions.explanation: Every real transfer wastes something — usually heat — so not all input can be useful.
questions.misconception: Perfection is a myth in physics; friction and losses are always present.

questions.prompt: Where does the wasted energy of a bulb mostly go?
options: Into heat that warms the bulb and room
Into more light it never gave
questions.explanation: Most 'wasted' energy becomes heat — which is why old bulbs glow hot and why conservation's total still balances.
questions.misconception: Repeating the disappearance myth ignores heat, the biggest single waste channel.

questions.prompt: Which change would raise a machine's efficiency?
questions.explanation: Cut losses and the same input produces more useful output — efficiency climbs.
questions.misconception: Topping up input or extra hardware can raise waste, not the useful share.
